execution.note: Several agents share one M5 GPU; bandwidth_control readings are reported per artifact to expose contention.

accepted: Tiled row-IFFT store for the scalar 512 loss path (engine.py:4607-4636 with plumbing at engine.py:2041 and engine.py:2917): 22.767 to 21.055 ms on the isolated stage pair, 404.0 to 369.5 ms end-to-end, bit-exact on three parameter triples.
Nothing new was accepted for the fit path: both named levers are closed by measurement (see leverage_ceilings).
findings.accumulate_first_verdict: Refuted for the objective by the atan2/variance nonlinearity (see rejected), so the loss cannot be rewritten as a single transform of a summed frequency-domain plane; the redraw path is the only place where accumulate-first is valid.
findings.bottleneck_verdict: The 8937-BF fit is device_memory-limited at the machine's streaming ceiling, with a large overlapped non-device_memory component: the batch-2 objective moves 84.376 GB in 647.0 ms = 130.4 GB/s against a same-session mx.array copy control of 126.3-132.3 GB/s, and the row stage alone moves 2,686,451,712 B in 20.347 ms = 132.0 GB/s. Removing its 538,968,064 B G read recovers 3.913 ms of 20.347 ms, exactly the read's 19.2% byte share. An intermediate 'co-limited' reading was recorded here and then withdrawn; the replacement measurement is in experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-colimit, which halves the row stage's write bytes with no aliasing and recovers 54.5% of the device_memory prediction, and which disproves the threadgroup-occupancy hypothesis with an order-balanced sweep (8 KB 24.846 ms, 16 KB 23.168 ms, 32 KB shipped 22.534 ms, all byte-identical).
findings.bottleneck_verdict_superseded: The 8937-BF fit is device_memory-traffic bound at the machine's streaming ceiling: the batch-2 objective moves 84.376 GB in 647.0 ms = 130.4 GB/s and the batch-1 objective 46.892 GB in 360.8 ms = 130.0 GB/s, against a same-session mx.array copy control of 126.3-132.3 GB/s. No sync, host round-trip, geometry or chunk-size term is measurable above noise.
findings.bottleneck_verdict_superseded_by_colimit: The 8937-BF fit is co-limited, not purely device_memory-bound. The byte accounting stands: the batch-2 objective moves 84.376 GB in 647.0 ms = 130.4 GB/s and the batch-1 objective 46.892 GB in 360.8 ms = 130.0 GB/s, against a same-session mx.array copy control of 126.3-132.3 GB/s, and no sync, host round-trip, geometry or chunk-size term is measurable above noise. But same-session stage ablations in experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-2pass-price show device_memory is not what binds: folding the row stage's plane write saves 1.71 ms of 20.38 ms and pinning the column stage's plane read saves 4.56 ms of 17.82 ms, while the row stage's own read:write mix allows 196.2 GB/s (1:4 broadcast control) against 131.8 GB/s achieved. Roughly 60-70% of each stage is therefore non-device_memory (correction ALU, butterfly issue and barriers at the 32 KB threadgroup occupancy), which supersedes this experiment's earlier 'at the streaming ceiling' reading.
findings.fit_change_verdict: f357069 (tiled scalar row IFFT) does not touch the fit objective path: a 4-trial fit calls _reconstruct_prepared 0 times and the batched row IFFT 1944 times (= 18 packs x 108 objectives), and the batched path was already tiled in the frozen tree. The paired fit A/B therefore shows only host drift (79.28 -> 77.72 s p50) while both objective paths are equal within noise (batch2 648.3 vs 647.0 ms, batch1 360.8 vs 359.2 ms). The change is an interactive redraw/scalar-loss win, not a fit win.
findings.fit_split_at_8937_bf: Fit wall 79.03 s = 200-trial loop 65.9 s (83.4%, 100 batch-2 calls at p50 653.3 ms = 3.06 candidates/s) + Nelder-Mead 11.4 s (14.4%, 31 batch-1 calls at p50 367.6 ms = 2.72 evals/s) + initial loss 0.44 s (0.6%) + final object/phase 0.52 s (0.7%); optuna bookkeeping adds 0.4 s (0.6%).

leverage_ceilings.batch_the_200_trials: Already batch-2 (engine.py:4924). Wider batches are re-tiled into pairs (engine.py:4955-4966) and the code records a measured 2.8x per-candidate regression at batch 4, so K=4 buys 0%. The arithmetic ceiling is the G share: 11.1% of per-candidate traffic at K=2, so K=4 would cap at 5.6% and K=infinite at 11.1% of the trial loop, i.e. 9.2% of the fit.
leverage_ceilings.reduce_intermediate_bytes: Measured closed in experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-2pass-price. Two independent reasons. (1) The plane carries no exact redundancy: 4.5-7.1% mirror residuals and |imag|/|real| = 0.036 on real 8937-BF data, so it cannot be stored smaller. (2) It cannot be avoided: fusion would have to hold the whole 2,097,152 B plane per threadgroup against a measured 32,768 B limit (64x), and the only tile that fits re-reads the input 64x. Ablating the intermediate's device_memory traffic entirely (row store folded to four planes, column read pinned to one plane) saves 1.71 ms of 20.38 ms and 4.56 ms of 17.82 ms, i.e. 6.27 ms of the ~35.7 ms per pack, 17% of the 79.0 s fit - an upper bound that is unreachable, not a lever.

ranked_bottlenecks: engine.py:4975 (pair pack loop) -> engine.py:2626 (tiled row store) -> engine.py:2337 (tiled column load): the row-IFFT intermediate round trip is 4.295 GB of the 4.834 GB moved per 512-BF pair pack (88.9%), i.e. 37.48 GB of the 42.19 GB per candidate at batch 2. That is a byte share, not a time share: experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-2pass-price ablates its device_memory traffic at 6.27 ms of the ~35.7 ms per pack, about 17% of the 79.0 s fit, and the round trip is not removable on this hardware.

engine.py:2660/2712 (G_qk read inside the row kernel) + engine.py:4834 (_pk_batch_from_prepared): the 9.408 GB half-plane G cache is 20.1% of a batch-1 candidate (9.41 GB) and 11.1% at batch 2 (4.70 GB/candidate).
engine.py:5080 (_nelder_mead_refine): 31 sequential batch-1 evaluations = 14.4% of the fit; each is one 46.89 GB objective, so the G read cannot be amortised across the simplex.

engine.py:3013 (per-element geometry) and engine.py:2438 (atan2 column stage): ablating sqrt+sincos from the row IFFT moves that stage 8% and ablating atan2 from the column stage moves it 5%, so compute is exposed but small.

engine.py:2958 (mx.eval per pack in the pair loop): 18 syncs per objective, required to bound the 2.15 GB pack buffers; measured depth A/B shows deeper pipelining is slower (391.5/397.5/399.5/481.5 ms at k=1..4).
findings.ranked_bottlenecks_superseded_0: engine.py:4975 (pair pack loop) -> engine.py:2626 (tiled row store) -> engine.py:2337 (tiled column load): the row-IFFT intermediate round trip is 4.295 GB of the 4.834 GB moved per 512-BF pair pack (88.9%), i.e. 37.48 GB of the 42.19 GB per candidate at batch 2. It is 86% of the fit wall.
rejected: Accumulating the candidate-weighted BF planes in the frequency domain before the transform (IFFT2(sum_bf c_bf(q) G_bf(q)) == sum_bf IFFT2(c_bf(q) G_bf(q))): refuted on the objective, not on precision. The loss is mean_pixel(Var_bf(phi)), a variance of the phase across BF terms, so a phase has to exist per BF term; the atan2 nonlinearity sits between the transform and the sum and sum_bf phi_bf != phi(sum_bf z_bf), so linearity does not apply. A second, independent barrier is that the Nyquist boundary correction is added inside the atan2 argument and is indexed by BF term. The redraw path really does accumulate first because its output is linear, which is why the idea looked general; it does not generalise to the loss.

Fusing the row and column stages so the intermediate round trip disappears (4,295 MB of the 4,834 MB per 512-BF pair pack): blocked by on-chip capacity, measured on this host in experiments/20260916-ssb-mps-2pass-price. The MLX/Metal threadgroup ceiling is 32,768 B (33,792 B refuses to load: 'Threadgroup memory size (33792) exceeds the maximum threadgroup memory allowed (32768)'), both engine kernels already reserve exactly 32,768 B, and the transformed plane is 2,097,152 B, 64x that. The only tile that fits, 512 rows x 8 columns, needs 64 threadgroups that each re-read the full input: 64x input amplification. Priced by ablation: removing the intermediate's device_memory traffic is worth 6.27 ms of the ~35.7-37.0 ms per pack, 17% of the fit wall (79.0 s -> about 65.6 s at 8937 BF), and any re-decomposition moves the pinned loss by about 8e-7 relative against the engine's own 1.2e-7 float32 floor.

Enabling the SIMD register transpose column stage on non-M5-Max hardware: bit-exact and 4.3% faster on that stage, but it changes a hardware-gated kernel path for devices that cannot be measured on this host.
Smaller or larger phase-loss chunk (512 to 256/1024): changes the float32 reduction grouping and is not bit-exact; measured 388-437 ms against 370-402 ms at 512.
Removing the per-chunk mx.eval: measured slower and higher peak memory.
Reducing the pair pack eval depth or re-packing BF boundaries: no peak-memory saving (MLX caches freed buffers) and slower batch2 (1028.1 ms at depth 1 vs 697.8 ms at depth 5).

Hoisting the per-element geometry into a table like the native Metal ssb_precompute_cross_trig: a per-(bf, row, col) table is 75 GB, and the separable form is a different float32 expression, so it cannot be bit-exact.

Hoisting the per-candidate geometry into a Metal-style cross_trig table: indexed by (row, col, bf) it is ~75 GB; a (dx, dy)-indexed table would need new per-element index arithmetic and still only recovers part of the measured 8%/5% ablation, so the payoff does not survive the bit-exactness cost.
Batching Nelder-Mead evaluations: the simplex is sequential and speculative reflect+expand batching would add wasted candidates for a <=5.6% amortisation of the smallest term in the fit.

verdict_on_suspected_causes.chunk_size_cliff: not on this 24 GB host: 512 BF is the measured optimum, and 1024 is not bit-exact.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.fit_host_round_trips: negligible: 7 evals and one host read per objective out of ~350 ms; the fit is 131 objective calls and nothing else.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.memory_or_compute_bound: memory bound at the ceiling (129-134 GB/s of a 125-130 GB/s copy ceiling), unlike the native Metal probe at 42 GB/s.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.per_chunk_sync: refuted twice: fewer syncs are slower and use more memory.
verdict_on_suspected_causes.repeated_geometry: real in the native Metal sense but not hoistable here without changing the float32 expression.

artifact_results.intermediate-redundancy: Real 512x512 complex64 row-IFFT plane, 2,097,152 B: no exact redundancy. Joint (q,c)->(512-q,512-c) mirror residual 45,715 = 4.8% of peak 954,211, row mirror 4.5%, column mirror 7.1%, max|imag|/max|real| 0.0356, so the plane cannot be halved or stored as real without approximation.
